questions.question_text: Which Virginia agency administers the Virginia Fair Housing Act?
questions.correct_answer: The Virginia Fair Housing Office within DPOR
distractors: The Virginia Real Estate Board only
The Virginia Attorney General's office
The local circuit court in each county
questions.explanation: The Virginia Fair Housing Law (Va. Code § 36-96.1 et seq.) is administered by the Fair Housing Board and the Real Estate Board through DPOR's Fair Housing Office, which takes and investigates complaints. Enforcement actions seeking civil penalties are brought by the Attorney General.

questions.question_text: A landlord refuses to rent to a tenant because the tenant plans to pay with a housing choice voucher. Under Virginia law, this is:
questions.correct_answer: Illegal discrimination based on source of funds
distractors: Legal because landlords choose payment methods
Legal unless the unit has federal funding
Illegal only if HUD files a complaint
questions.explanation: Va. Code § 36-96.3 lists source of funds among Virginia's protected classes, and the definition covers housing choice vouchers and other lawful sources of rent payment. Refusing to rent solely because of voucher use violates state law even though federal law has no such class.

questions.question_text: Virginia's Fair Housing Act protects 'elderliness' as a class. What minimum age qualifies?
distractors: 62 years of age or older
65 years of age or older
60 years of age or older
questions.explanation: Va. Code § 36-96.1:1 defines elderliness as an individual who has attained his fifty-fifth birthday, making age 55 and older a Virginia-specific protected class in housing.

questions.question_text: A property manager tells a same-sex couple that no units are available, though vacancies exist. Under Virginia fair housing law, this violates protections for:
distractors: Familial status only
Marital status under federal law
No violation under Virginia law
questions.explanation: Sexual orientation and gender identity were added to Va. Code § 36-96.3 in 2020. Representing that no dwelling is available when one is, because of a protected characteristic, is prohibited.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a Virginia-specific protected class NOT found in federal fair housing law?
distractors: National origin
Disability
Familial status
questions.explanation: Virginia's twelve protected classes under Va. Code § 36-96.3 are race, color, religion, national origin, sex, elderliness, familial status, source of funds, sexual orientation, gender identity, military status, and disability. Military status, elderliness, source of funds, sexual orientation, and gender identity are the state-only additions.

questions.question_text: A real estate agent steers minority buyers away from certain neighborhoods. The seller instructs the agent to do so. Under Virginia law, the agent should:
questions.correct_answer: Refuse because agents cannot follow such orders
distractors: Follow the seller's lawful instruction
Comply but document the seller's request
Report the seller but still comply
questions.explanation: Steering is prohibited by Va. Code § 36-96.3 regardless of who directs it, and a licensee has an independent duty to comply with fair housing law under Va. Code § 54.1-2131. A client's instruction is no defense.

questions.question_text: Under Virginia's Fair Housing Act, what is the maximum civil penalty for a first offense of housing discrimination?
questions.explanation: In a civil action brought by the Attorney General under Va. Code § 36-96.17, the court may assess a civil penalty not exceeding $50,000 for a first violation and not exceeding $100,000 for any subsequent violation. A private action under § 36-96.18 has no such cap on compensatory and punitive damages.

questions.question_text: The Mrs. Murphy exemption in Virginia fair housing law applies to owner-occupied dwellings with how many or fewer units?
distractors: Two units or fewer
Three units or fewer
Six units or fewer
questions.explanation: Va. Code § 36-96.2 B exempts rooms or units in dwellings occupied by no more than four families living independently where the owner actually occupies one of the units. The exemption never applies to a Real Estate Board licensee or Fair Housing Board regulant, and discriminatory advertising is prohibited regardless.

questions.question_text: A Virginia respondent is found liable in a second Attorney General fair housing action. What is the maximum civil penalty the court may assess?
questions.explanation: Va. Code § 36-96.17 authorizes a civil penalty of up to $50,000 for a first violation and up to $100,000 for any subsequent violation. Unlike the federal scheme, Virginia's statute attaches no look-back period to the word 'subsequent.'

questions.question_text: A buyer believes they experienced housing discrimination in Virginia. Where may they file a complaint?
questions.correct_answer: VA Fair Housing Office, HUD, or private lawsuit
distractors: Only with the Virginia Real Estate Board
Only with the local police department
Only through a federal court action
questions.explanation: Va. Code § 36-96.9 and § 36-96.18 allow a complaint to DPOR's Fair Housing Office, a complaint to HUD under the federal Fair Housing Act, or a private civil action — the last of which may be filed regardless of whether an administrative complaint was made.

questions.question_text: All real estate advertising in Virginia must be placed under whose supervision?
questions.correct_answer: The principal or supervising broker of the firm
distractors: The individual licensee placing the ad
The Virginia Real Estate Board
The local association of Realtors
questions.explanation: 18VAC135-20-190 A requires all advertising to be under the direct supervision of the principal broker or supervising broker and in the name of the firm, with the firm's licensed name clearly and legibly displayed.

questions.question_text: A Virginia licensee creates a social media ad featuring only her name with no firm name. This is:
questions.correct_answer: A prohibited blind ad under Virginia law
distractors: Acceptable if her license number appears
Permitted for personal social media accounts
Legal if she adds the firm name later
questions.explanation: 18VAC135-20-190 requires every advertisement by a firm or affiliated licensee to display the firm's licensed name clearly and legibly and to carry an advertising disclosure containing the firm's name and office contact information. An ad identifying only the individual licensee is the classic blind ad and violates the rule.

questions.question_text: A team within a Virginia brokerage advertises using only the team name. What rule does this violate?
questions.correct_answer: Firm name must appear in all team advertising
distractors: Teams cannot advertise in Virginia
Only the team leader's name may appear
Team ads require Board pre-approval
questions.explanation: 18VAC135-20-190 A requires all advertising to be in the name of the firm with the firm's licensed name clearly and legibly displayed, and 190 B requires the advertising disclosure with the firm name and office contact information. A team may advertise under its own name only if the firm is identified too.

questions.question_text: A Virginia agent advertises a property guaranteeing the buyer will profit from appreciation. This advertising is:
distractors: Allowed if market data supports the claim
Permitted with a written disclaimer
Legal if the broker approves the ad
questions.explanation: 18VAC135-20-300 prohibits making false promises through advertising and knowingly making material misrepresentations. Values can fall, so guaranteeing appreciation misleads consumers.

questions.question_text: Under 18VAC135-20-190, what must the advertising disclosure on every Virginia real estate advertisement contain?
questions.correct_answer: The firm's name and the office contact information
distractors: The licensee's license number and expiration date
The principal broker's personal name and cell number
The local Board of Realtors name and logo
questions.explanation: 18VAC135-20-190 B requires all advertising by a firm or affiliated licensee to contain a clear, legible, and conspicuous advertising disclosure consisting of the firm's name and the office contact information, with the broker specifying the contact details in written policy. Virginia's rule has no test comparing the relative prominence or type size of the licensee's name against the firm's.
